name: Young adult novel
hint: For ages 13 and up: a lie that grows, a friend group that cracks and a choice the protagonist makes entirely alone. Each step often becomes two or three chapters.

parts.title: Before
chapters: An ordinary day
Open on a scene where the protagonist wants something and something is already wrong, with no background lecture.
What throws everything
An event they can't ignore: a new school, a secret, a broken promise.
The decision
They choose to get involved, for a reason the reader recognises from their own life.

parts.title: New rules
chapters: New people
A new friend, a rival or a group that opens up another world and makes new demands.
The first time
The first party, the first kiss or the first lie to a parent: something new that they feel everywhere and can't take back.
Belonging
What they have to do or hide to be part of it, and what that costs someone else.
The lie grows
What they're hiding gets bigger and harder to back out of. End the chapter close to discovery.

parts.title: Everything breaks
chapters: The midpoint
A victory that turns out to be false, or a truth that changes the game.
The price
Friends, family or their sense of self pay for the protagonist's choices.
Found out
The lie comes out in front of the people who matter most, and the protagonist stands alone.
Rock bottom
They see their own part in what happened. No adult arrives to save the day.

parts.title: After
chapters: The choice
They decide who they want to be, and do something hard to prove it.
The deciding moment
The protagonist resolves the conflict by their own means, not by luck or a parent.
Who they became
An ending with hope: what has changed, and what is allowed to stay unresolved.

name: Middle-grade novel
hint: For ages 9 to 12: a problem the adults can't solve, a friend with a will of their own and a subplot at home. Sixteen chapters of just under 2,000 words.

parts.title: The start
chapters: An ordinary day
Show the protagonist at home or at school, what they want and what is already wrong, with action from the first line.
Something happens
Something unexpected upsets everyday life: a discovery, some news, a new pupil. End on a question.
Why no adult
Show why the adults can't or mustn't help, so the problem becomes the protagonist's own.
The decision
They decide to do something themselves, and take the first step before the chapter ends.

parts.title: Trying
chapters: The friend
A friend or a reluctant helper joins in, with goals of their own that aren't the protagonist's.
The first attempt
The plan almost works. Give a small win and a new obstacle.
At home
The subplot: a sibling, a parent or a rival makes life harder and mirrors the main problem.
The secret
The protagonist hides something from someone who matters a lot, and it starts to cost.

parts.title: The darkest point
chapters: The midpoint
A discovery changes everything: the problem is bigger, or different from what they thought.
The falling-out
The friends quarrel, and the protagonist is partly to blame.
Everything goes wrong
The plan falls apart in front of others, the secret comes out and they stand alone.
What they already know
Alone with it, they remember something from earlier in the book that points to a way out.

parts.title: All the way
chapters: Sorry
They seek out the friend and own their part, before the deciding moment.
The new plan
A plan built on their own strength and on the friend, not on luck.
The deciding moment
The protagonist solves the problem by their own means. The adults may come in afterwards, not before.
Back again
A hopeful ending in a scene that mirrors the opening and shows what is different now.

name: Chapter book for children
hint: For ages 6 to 9: ten short chapters with a hook in each, an adventure, and a problem the child solves on their own.

chapters: At home
The protagonist, what they wish for, and something funny or strange on the very first page.
Something happens
A surprise sets everything going. End the chapter on a question the reader wants answered.
The plan
The protagonist makes up their mind and makes a plan, ideally with a friend.
Into the unknown
The adventure begins, and at first it goes better than expected.
The first obstacle
Something goes wrong. Solve it halfway and let a new problem appear.
The falling-out
The friends quarrel or the plan falls apart. End so the child simply has to know what happens.
The hard part
The problem seems too big, and there's no adult around.
Brave enough
The protagonist works out the solution alone, using something they learned earlier in the book.
The solution
The plan is carried out, with one last surprise or a laugh.
Home again
Safe, but not quite as before. Show what they've learned without saying it.
